overview: Prologis is the world's largest owner, operator, and developer of logistics real estate, with investments in roughly 5,900+ buildings totaling approximately 1.3 billion square feet across 20 countries on four continents, leased to about 6,500 customers. The company operates a dual-engine model: a wholly/majority-owned real estate portfolio generating rental income, plus a Strategic Capital segment that manages co-investment ventures with institutional partners (approximately $230 billion of total assets under management at year-end 2025), earning recurring fees and performance promotes. Prologis is also expanding into higher-and-better-use conversions of logistics land into data centers to capture AI/power-driven demand, and in August 2026 agreed to acquire UK-listed SEGRO plc for approximately $18.8 billion, a transformative expansion of its European footprint.

business_model.summary: Prologis earns the large majority of revenue from rental income on owned/consolidated logistics real estate, supplemented by fee and promote income from managing co-investment ventures on behalf of institutional capital partners (the Strategic Capital segment), plus smaller development management and other income. The co-investment model lets Prologis control far more real estate than its balance sheet alone would support, while recycling capital (contributing stabilized assets into ventures, redeploying proceeds into higher-return development) and earning asset-management fees and promotes on top of its retained ownership stake.
business_model.customer_type: B2B — diverse base of ~6,500 tenants spanning e-commerce/retail fulfillment, third-party logistics (3PL), transportation, food & beverage, and general business-to-business distribution; largest tenant Amazon at roughly 4-5% of net effective rent, with no other tenant above ~2%
business_model.geographic_mix: Primarily U.S. (majority of NOI), with meaningful operations in Europe (Germany, UK, France, etc.), Mexico/Brazil, and Asia (Japan, China, India); European exposure set to expand materially upon completion of the SEGRO acquisition

main_competitors: Blackstone (private industrial platform, e.g., Link Logistics)
competitive_position.market_position: Dominant global leader in logistics real estate by a wide margin — market capitalization roughly 10x+ that of the next-largest listed pure-play peer (EastGroup, ~$11B). Serves an estimated ~40% of the Fortune 500 as tenants and holds the largest enterprise value among public REITs globally.

moat_factors.description: Multinational tenants (Amazon, Home Depot, FedEx, DHL, Geodis) sign portfolio-wide leases across markets/geographies that only a global platform like Prologis can service
Concentrated in supply-constrained, high-growth infill markets near population centers and ports, where entitlement and zoning barriers limit new competing supply
~$230B AUM lets Prologis control far more real estate than its own balance sheet, generating high-margin recurring fee income and promotes while recycling capital into higher-return development
Investment-grade balance sheet and scale give Prologis access to cheaper debt/equity than smaller peers, supporting accretive acquisitions and development
5.8 GW power pipeline (1.7GW secured, 3.9GW advanced stage) built on existing land bank creates a differentiated higher-and-better-use conversion opportunity vs. pure industrial peers

weaknesses: Premium valuation (trades at a premium multiple to peers) raises the bar for continued outperformance
Large scale makes incremental growth harder to achieve organically; increasingly reliant on development and M&A (e.g., SEGRO) for growth
Execution and integration risk from the large SEGRO acquisition and data-center capex ramp
Industrial sector-wide oversupply risk in certain submarkets from a multi-year development boom

growth_drivers: Secular e-commerce penetration and supply-chain modernization driving sustained demand for modern logistics space
Record leasing activity and rising occupancy (95.5% as of Q2 2026, up 20bps QoQ) supporting continued rent growth (cash same-store NOI guided 6.75-7.25% for 2026)
Conversion of logistics land into data centers, leveraging a 5.8 GW power pipeline to capture AI/hyperscaler demand at premium economics
Development pipeline funded via build-to-suit and speculative starts ($5.5-6.5B guided for 2026), recycled through Strategic Capital co-investment ventures
SEGRO acquisition (agreed August 2026, ~$18.8B, expected to close H1 2027) expanding European logistics/data-center land bank by ~126% and bringing combined AUM to ~$269B
Growing Strategic Capital fee pool as AUM expands via new ventures with partners such as GIC and La Caisse
Rent mark-to-market opportunity as in-place rents reset toward higher market rents on expiring leases

business.description: Multi-year development boom across the sector (Prologis alone guiding $5.5-6.5B of 2026 starts) risks elevated vacancy and weaker pricing power in some submarkets, particularly after a period of outsized rent growth

Amazon is the largest tenant (~4-5% of net effective rent); normalization of pandemic-era e-commerce demand growth could slow absorption, though overall tenant concentration remains low (top 5 tenants ~10% of rent)

The pivot toward a reported ~$25B AI data-center buildout is unproven at this scale for Prologis, with power/grid constraints, local community opposition, and speculative-building dynamics introducing new project risk
The ~$18.8B SEGRO acquisition (expected to close H1 2027) is Prologis's largest-ever deal, carrying integration, cultural, and portfolio-overlap execution risk across European markets

financial.description: Net debt/EBITDA around 5.2x and debt/equity of 0.64x; funding a large development pipeline plus the SEGRO acquisition (partly via share issuance, partly cash) could pressure the balance sheet or dilute existing shareholders
Operations across 20 countries (Europe, Mexico, Brazil, Japan, China, India) create FX translation risk on both revenue and the SEGRO deal, which includes a GBP cash-alternative component

As a capital-intensive REIT reliant on debt and equity markets to fund acquisitions/development, Prologis's cost of capital and valuation multiple are sensitive to interest-rate moves and cap-rate expansion/compression

regulatory.description: SEGRO acquisition requires UK court sanction of the scheme, shareholder approval, and regulatory clearances; any delay or imposed condition could push back the H1 2027 expected close

regulatory.risk: REIT tax status and local property/energy regulation
regulatory.description: Maintaining REIT qualification is required for favorable tax treatment; data-center and energy infrastructure buildout also introduces exposure to local utility and permitting regulation

macro.description: REIT valuations and property cap rates are highly sensitive to the rate environment; rising rates can compress valuations and raise financing costs for development and acquisitions
Tariff uncertainty and shifting global trade flows can affect tenant demand for logistics space, particularly in markets tied to import/export activity
A pullback in consumer spending or industrial production would reduce demand for warehouse and distribution space, as seen in softer occupancy in some Asia and Central Pennsylvania submarkets

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Logistics real estate demand remains supported by structural e-commerce growth, supply-chain reconfiguration (nearshoring, inventory buffer-building), and a new secular driver in AI/data-center land conversion; near-term supply growth in some markets is a watch item after several years of elevated construction
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate — industrial/logistics demand correlates with consumption, trade volumes, and industrial production, but Prologis's infill, high-barrier locations and diversified tenant base dampen cyclicality relative to other commercial real estate
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High — as a REIT, PLD's cost of capital, development funding, and valuation multiple (cap rate) are directly tied to interest rate levels and expectations
key_input_costs: Cost of debt and equity capital
Energy/power procurement costs tied to data-center buildout

recent_developments.event: Prologis announced a recommended acquisition of SEGRO plc for approximately $18.8 billion (0.0920 new Prologis shares per SEGRO share plus a partial cash alternative), expected to close H1 2027; combined company would manage ~$269B of AUM and expand the European land bank by ~126%

Q2 2026 results: record leasing of over 67 million square feet, occupancy of 95.5% (+20bps QoQ), Core FFO per share of $1.63 (vs. $1.46 prior year), same-store cash NOI growth of 8.5%; management raised full-year 2026 guidance for the second time this year

Leadership transition completed: Hamid Moghadam stepped down as CEO (after 40+ years leading the company and its predecessor AMB Property) to become Executive Chairman; Dan Letter, previously President, became CEO effective January 1, 2026

Prologis expanded its data center power pipeline to 5.8 GW (1.7GW secured including 423MW under development, 3.9GW advanced stage) and started roughly $1.3B of data center build-to-suits in Q1 2026, underscoring the AI/hyperscaler-driven pivot

Formed three new co-investment ventures with third-party investors (two U.S. development vehicles, one Asia acquisition vehicle), including expanded partnerships with sovereign/pension capital such as GIC and La Caisse
Analyst price targets have generally risen through the year (range roughly $123-$170) following the raised guidance and SEGRO deal announcement; consensus rating remains Moderate Buy

items.notes: Raised from prior guidance of $3.80-$4.05; second guidance raise of 2026
Reflects record leasing volume and improving fundamentals
Strong embedded rent mark-to-market continuing to flow through
Separate from the pending SEGRO transaction, which is expected to close H1 2027

guidance.management_commentary: Management characterized Q2 2026 as an 'exceptional quarter' with record leasing activity and the second guidance raise of the year, citing improving occupancy and strong cash same-store NOI growth. New CEO Dan Letter has also highlighted power constraints and local community resistance as emerging hurdles for the data-center pipeline, even as the company continues to scale its power position (5.8 GW pipeline) and pursue the transformative SEGRO acquisition to expand its European footprint and AUM.

bull_case: Unmatched global scale and infill land positions provide a durable moat and pricing power that smaller peers cannot replicate
Record leasing, rising occupancy, and raised guidance (twice in 2026) show the logistics demand cycle is reaccelerating, not decelerating
Data center/power pipeline (5.8 GW) offers a differentiated, high-return optionality on AI infrastructure demand layered on top of existing land holdings
SEGRO acquisition meaningfully expands European exposure and AUM (~$269B combined), reinforcing Prologis's position as the largest global logistics real estate platform
Strategic Capital segment generates high-margin, capital-light recurring fee and promote income that diversifies earnings beyond rental income
bear_case: Premium valuation relative to peers leaves little room for error, especially given a large, unproven data-center capital commitment (reportedly ~$25B planned)
Industrial/logistics sector faces supply growth risk after years of elevated development; oversupply in specific submarkets could cap rent growth and pressure occupancy
SEGRO acquisition carries material integration, financing, and cross-border regulatory execution risk, with completion not expected until H1 2027
High sensitivity to interest rates and cap rates means a renewed rate-hiking cycle or risk-off environment could compress valuation multiples
E-commerce demand normalization post-COVID and tariff/trade-policy uncertainty could slow the pace of leasing and absorption that has driven recent guidance raises
